items.stem:
Read the following extract on Sanskritisation and Westernisation and answer the questions that follow.
"Westernisation includes the adoption of Western dress, food, manners and ideas. Sanskritisation was a way of upward mobility within the caste hierarchy. Sanskritisation leads to positional changes but not structural change in caste."
(i) Which of these is a criticism of Sanskritisation? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'Westernisation' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Sanskritisation can worsen the status of women. (2)
items.answer: (i) It treats the upper-caste way of life as superior (ii) M.N. Srinivas's term for the changes in Indian society and culture resulting from over 150 years of British rule, in technology, institutions, ideology and values. (iii) Lower castes adopt upper-caste practices such as dowry in place of bride price and restrictions on women.

items.stem: Distinguish between 'Brahmo Samaj' and 'Arya Samaj'.
items.answer: Brahmo Samaj: the reform society founded by Raja Rammohun Roy in Bengal, which opposed sati and idol worship. Arya Samaj: the reform society founded by Dayanand Saraswati in 1875, which promoted Vedic ideals and education.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'Brahmo Samaj' (the reform society founded by Raja Rammohun Roy in Bengal, which opposed sati and idol worship.) and 1 mark for 'Arya Samaj' (the reform society founded by Dayanand Saraswati in 1875, which promoted Vedic ideals and education.), with the contrast between them made clear.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about modernisation and secularisation:
I. Modernisation involves the spread of rational thinking and scientific outlook.
II. Modernisation means the complete disappearance of tradition in India.
III. In modern societies, status is increasingly achieved rather than ascribed.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and III only
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is incorrect: Tradition and modernity coexist and influence each other. III is correct.
options: I and III only
III only
II only

items.stem:
Read the following extract on modernisation and secularisation and answer the questions that follow.
"Modernisation involves the spread of rational thinking and scientific outlook. Rituals can acquire secular dimensions, such as being occasions for social networking and display of status. Secularisation implies a decline in the influence of religion in public life."
(i) Modernisation refers to: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'universalism' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Caste has adapted to modern democratic politics. (2)
items.answer: (i) a shift to rational thinking, new technology and universal values (ii) The idea that rules and values apply equally to all, rather than depending on birth or group. (iii) Caste groups form associations and use their numbers to bargain for political power.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Reform movements were not uniform; some looked to Western ideas while others reinterpreted tradition. Reformers used modern ideas of liberalism and freedom along with traditional texts to argue for change. New modes of communication such as the printing press, telegraph and railways helped spread reform ideas. Nineteenth-century reformers opposed sati, child marriage and the ban on widow remarriage."
(i) Explain the term 'Brahmo Samaj', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Social reform movements spread rapidly in the 19th century. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Social reform movements began only after independence." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The reform society founded by Raja Rammohun Roy in Bengal, which opposed sati and idol worship. (ii) New modes of communication such as the printing press, telegraph and railways helped ideas travel. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: They began in the 19th century during colonial rule.
